/code-review 1

You are reviewing pull request #1 of this repository (dkropachev/ironweave) - a C++ project. The PR branch `rpc-stream-close-send-window` is checked out and its base branch is `main`, so the change under review is exactly `git diff main...HEAD`. Read the PR's own title and description first with `gh pr view 1`. Report EVERY finding you are confident in, each with: the file and line, a one-line title, a severity, and the reason it is wrong. result:
Reviewed `git diff main...HEAD` (3 commits: the `_stream_closing` guard, the reproducer test, the docs). The core fix is sound — I traced the `_outgoing_queue_ready` steal against `withdraw()`/`stop_send_loop()`'s promise-swapping and it still terminates; `_sink_closed_future` correctly covers the drain that `stop_send_loop()` no longer waits for; `stream_close()` can only run once and is mutually exclusive with `stop_send_loop()` via `_error`; the `_connected->write_buf` deref in the new deferred continuation cannot see a nullopt `_connected` (the only way `queue_drained` resolves is via `_negotiated`, which is only set after `set_socket()`, or exceptionally from `stop_send_loop()` which first sets `_error` and so prevents `stream_close()` from being entered). Test ordering is deterministic too — `make_stream_sink()` awaits the parent connection before creating the stream client, so `hooks.back()` is reliably the stream's hook.

Two findings:

- `tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:1883` — `test_data_sink_impl` only implements the `SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9` `put(std::span<...>)` overload; at API levels 7/8 (supported by `CMakeLists.txt:72` and `configure.py --api-level`) `data_sink_impl::put(net::packet)` is still pure virtual, so the class is abstract and the `override` refers to nothing — hard compile error. `tests/unit/loopback_socket.hh:144` guards the identical override with `#if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9`; CI only builds the default level, so this would only bite non-default builds.
- `src/rpc/rpc.cc:562` — `stream_close()` now defers `stop()` (and therefore `abort()`/`shutdown_input()`) behind the outgoing-queue drain. Previously `write_buf.close()` returned promptly even with a write in flight (that was the bug), and the immediate `stop()` is what eventually got `stop_send_loop()` to call `shutdown_output()` and break a stalled send. Now a send stalled on a full send window (e.g. a compressor empty frame, with the peer no longer draining) leaves `sink.close()` / the source read hung until the connection is aborted from outside.

One non-finding worth noting: the change leaves `_outgoing_queue_ready` as a ready future while entries can still be linked in `_outgoing_queue`, breaking the invariant that it is the tail entry's `done` future. Nothing enqueues after that point today (`send()` is refused, `enqueue_zero_frame()` only runs from the client ctor), but any future enqueue path that misses the `_stream_closing` check would fire immediately and re-open exactly the race this PR fixes.
